gen-playfair-display-fs-epilogue: Epilogue is all curves and wiry, uniform lines, with stubby ascenders. Playfair Display above it throws hairlines against fat strokes, so a long page moves from dramatic to relaxed.
gen-playfair-display-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans keeps its strokes sturdy, with a big x-height and no thin-thick swings inside a word. And Playfair Display earns its place large and brief, where those hairlines can be seen.
gen-playfair-display-fs-ranade: Organic and literary at once, this pairing runs from sharp to soft. Playfair Display does its best work with bold strokes against hairlines; Ranade just nudges its weight and spaces its stroke ends far apart.
gen-playfair-display-montserrat: Playfair Display brings hairline strokes and fat ones, with open mouths on its letters, to a dignified heading. Montserrat then glides along, spacious around every curve.
gen-poppins-fs-karma: Karma has a calm, classic serif voice with terminals that stop clear of the stem. Poppins heads it with uniform, wire-thin strokes, so a long page slides from geometric to gently modulated without a snag.
gen-press-start-2p-fs-rowan: Rowan is a friendly, literary serif with generous curves. Press Start 2P sits above it, chunky and retro, while the body's thin and thick strokes carry a long page softly.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-alumni-sans: Arcade pixels meet slim, tidy letters. Press Start 2P spreads its widely spaced characters out for fun, whereas Alumni Sans keeps ascenders low and its thick-thin contrast understated.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-cossette-titre: Retro pixel blocks sit over snug, low-profile text, each letter nestled close to the next. Press Start 2P is at its best big and brief, and Cossette Titre follows.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-headland-one: Old arcade charm over a dignified serif. Headland One has gently varied strokes and well-spaced letters, and next to Press Start 2P it brings a traditional gravity that makes the fun feel deliberate.
gen-press-start-2p-rubik: Soft and playful, Press Start 2P gives a retro, pixel-spaced heading with light modulation. And Rubik answers with big lowercase and round, open letters, which makes the fun feel easy to read.
